documents.title: Empirical Behavioral Dynamics in the Global South
documents.summary: Behavioral interventions in the Global South often require contextual adaptation around scarcity, trust, social observability, gendered time poverty, and structural constraints.
documents.text: Recurring themes include relational rather than systemic trust, the limits of light-touch cognitive reframing under scarcity, the context-dependent effects of social norms, gendered domestic and participation frictions, and the need to adapt Western behavioral assumptions to local realities.
documents.source: User-provided synthesis: Empirical Behavioral Dynamics in the Global South
works_when: trusted local intermediaries or visible verification are available
the behavior is socially visible and peers are relevant to the decision
fails_when: messages only shift beliefs while practical barriers remain
peer norms substitute for objective feedback or individual accountability
design ignores time poverty, safety, dignity, or household power dynamics
documents.design_implication: Build around trusted local intermediaries and visible verification rather than assuming institutional or digital trust is enough.

documents.title: Analog Visual Progress Tracking for Digital Savings
documents.summary: Pairing SMS reminders with physical progress trackers can increase savings more effectively than digital reminders alone.
documents.text: Physical tools such as visual progress trackers act as persistent reminders that reduce cognitive load and keep savings goals salient during high-expenditure periods. This supports the broader finding that tangible, analog nudges can outperform purely digital prompts when users face scarcity and attention constraints.
works_when: the cue arrives close to the moment of action
digital attention is weak or cognitive load is high
documents.design_implication: Use reminders and persistent cues at the moment of action, especially when attention is scarce or routines are crowded.

documents.title: Group Pre-Commitment Devices and Savings Vouchers in Cash Transfer Programs
documents.summary: Physical pre-commitment boxes and weekly savings vouchers increase collective micro-savings among cash transfer beneficiaries.
documents.text: In Nigeria, the Household Uplifting Programme enrolled 297,973 households across 20 states. Participants were provided with a physical box where they collectively defined a group savings target, and individual members allocated savings vouchers over an eight-week period to represent committed funds. This increased savings to an average of 1,311 Naira per member, compared to 1,081 Naira in the control group, leveraging group accountability and pre-commitment to counter present bias.
documents.effect_size: increased savings to an average of 1,311 Naira
works_when: participants can make commitments concrete and revisit them repeatedly
digital attention is weak or cognitive load is high
documents.design_implication: Use concrete commitment artifacts, public accountability, and repeated group rituals to help people protect future intent under present bias.

documents.title: Social Signaling via Paper Savings Tokens in Collective Meetings
documents.summary: Depositing low-cost physical tokens during savings meetings acts as a strong social signal that increases group savings.
documents.text: In the Nigerian Household Uplifting Programme, paper savings tokens were deposited into labeled savings funds during weekly meetings. Although the tokens held no monetary value, depositing them publicly signaled savings intent to peers. This increased average individual savings to 1,190 Naira compared to 1,081 Naira in the control group.
documents.effect_size: increased average individual savings to 1,190 Naira
works_when: the savings intent is publicly visible to relevant peers
groups already meet regularly and can observe contributions
fails_when: public signaling creates shame without a realistic path to save
documents.design_implication: Use visible, low-cost tokens to make savings intent observable in trusted group settings without requiring immediate cash movement.

documents.title: Labeling Mismatch and the Frictions of Growth Champions in Savings Groups
documents.summary: Assigning formal accountability roles without structural support can backfire and decrease collective savings.
documents.text: In Nigerian conditional cash transfer savings groups, designated Growth Champions were expected to convene meetings, recruit members, and enforce savings consistency. The intervention reduced average savings to 779 Naira compared to 1,081 Naira in the control group, suggesting that formal top-down leadership labels can create social friction, pressure, or resentment without underlying support.
documents.effect_size: reduced average savings to 779 Naira
works_when: leadership labels are paired with resources, training, legitimacy, and cash-flow flexibility
fails_when: formal labels create pressure without resources, training, or legitimacy
documents.design_implication: Treat this as a cautionary case: match behavioral labels and messages with structural support, local trust, and operational capacity before scaling.

documents.title: Relative-Rank Social Messaging for Mobile Money Savings
documents.summary: Weekly relative-rank SMS updates comparing users to immediate peers drive higher digital savings than generic or agency-based messages.
documents.text: A lab-in-the-field study in informal settlements of Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, with CGAP and Airtel Money evaluated mobile savings nudges. Relative-rank messages showed users their savings rank within a cohort and the savings rate of peers two ranks ahead. This achievable comparison increased savings balances, while agency and financial-control messages performed worse than control.
works_when: peer comparison is achievable and peers feel relevant to the user
fails_when: messages emphasize abstract personal agency instead of concrete peer benchmarks
documents.design_implication: Make the target behavior visible to relevant peers, but pair peer pressure with clear accountability when performance quality matters.

documents.title: Active-Choice Framing for Digital Credit Terms and Conditions
documents.summary: Requiring borrowers to actively choose to view or skip summary terms and conditions increases readership by 16% and reduces delinquency.
documents.text: An onboarding experiment for digital credit products in Kenya required borrowers to actively choose whether to view or skip a summary screen of key terms. This increased terms and conditions readership by 16%. A required summary of terms later reduced absolute loan delinquency rates by 7%, highlighting the value of attention salience in borrowing decisions.
documents.effect_size: increased terms and conditions readership by 16%
works_when: the cue arrives close to the moment of action
documents.design_implication: Require borrowers to make an explicit view-or-skip choice for key loan terms so attention is directed to repayment obligations before borrowing.

documents.title: Unbundling and Cost Salience in Digital Loan App Menus
documents.summary: Separating loan principal from finance charges in digital menus reduces default rates from 29.1% to 20%.
documents.text: A laboratory borrowing simulation in Nairobi found that separating principal repayments from finance charges reduced consumer default from 29.1% to 20%. Cost salience mitigates cognitive load and prevents borrowers from overestimating repayment capacity under liquidity constraints.
documents.effect_size: reduced consumer default from 29.1%
works_when: users face complex prices, fees, or repayment tradeoffs
interfaces can separate principal, fees, and total repayment clearly
fails_when: users lack enough liquidity to repay even after costs become salient
documents.design_implication: Separate principal, fees, and total repayment obligations in digital credit menus to reduce computational burden.

documents.title: Social Observability and Peer Exposure in Public Health Compliance
documents.summary: Removing confidentiality and exposing individuals to peers at communal standpipes dramatically increases handwashing rates.
documents.text: A public health pilot at communal water standpipes in Kawangware, Kenya, found baseline handwashing was only 8% in the absence of peer observability. Introducing peer exposure or removing confidentiality increased compliance, suggesting reputation and concern for negative health externalities can be strong low-cost levers.
works_when: the behavior affects others and compliance is visible at the point of action
fails_when: observability creates stigma or avoidance instead of constructive accountability
documents.design_implication: Make the target behavior visible to relevant peers, but pair peer pressure with clear accountability when performance quality matters.

documents.title: The Information-Action Gap in Water Chlorination Interventions
documents.summary: Purely informational campaigns shift beliefs but fail to increase water chlorination or reduce diarrhea rates.
documents.text: An RCT among 3,750 young women in rural Kenya found that information on chlorine benefits shifted beliefs but had no statistical effect on chlorination rates or diarrhea incidence. This shows that belief change is insufficient when physical, cognitive, or self-efficacy barriers remain.
documents.effect_size: no statistical effect on chlorination rates or diarrhea incidence
works_when: information is paired with reduced hassle costs, self-efficacy, or physical access
fails_when: messages only shift beliefs while practical barriers remain
documents.design_implication: Design around time poverty, dignity, safety, and intra-household permission constraints rather than treating access as gender-neutral.

documents.title: Cross-Cultural Frictions and Failure of the TSST-G in Kenya
documents.summary: The standardized Western Trier Social Stress Test for Groups fails to induce subjective stress in Kenyan cohorts.
documents.text: Laboratory studies at the Busara Center in Nairobi found that the TSST-G public-speaking stressor did not increase subjective stress or temporal discounting among Kenyan participants, and in some sessions decreased subjective stress. Physical and economic stressors were more effective, showing that Western stress protocols require contextual validation.
works_when: behavioral protocols are locally validated before being used for inference
fails_when: Western protocols are assumed to induce the same psychological state across cultures
documents.design_implication: Validate behavioral protocols locally before drawing conclusions from Western-designed stress or decision-making tasks.

documents.title: Long-Term Economic and Well-Being Spillovers of Cash Transfers
documents.summary: Unconditional cash transfers yield sustained asset gains after three years but can create negative economic spillovers for non-recipients within the same village.
documents.text: A randomized evaluation of GiveDirectly's unconditional cash transfers in rural Kenya found recipients sustained a 40% increase in asset holdings after three years. Non-recipients in treatment villages experienced a 16% reduction in monthly consumption and lower psychological well-being, likely due to local market spillovers and asset sales.
works_when: cash transfer design monitors village-level spillovers and local market effects
fails_when: recipient gains are evaluated without measuring non-recipient neighbors
documents.design_implication: Adapt the mechanism to local scarcity, trust, channel, and population constraints before applying it to a new campaign.

documents.title: Short-Term UCT Impact on Asset Holdings and Consumption
documents.summary: Unconditional cash transfers in Kenya drove a 23% increase in monthly consumption and a 58.3% increase in asset holdings.
documents.text: GiveDirectly unconditional cash transfers in western Kenya increased monthly consumption from $158 PPP to $193 PPP and asset holdings by $302 PPP, largely through livestock, furniture, and metal roofing. The evidence suggests that large wealth shocks can improve short-term material welfare without increasing temptation-good spending, though longer-term equilibrium effects need attention.
documents.effect_size: increased monthly consumption from $158 PPP to $193 PPP and asset holdings by $302 PPP, largely through livestock, furniture, and metal roofing
works_when: material deprivation is the primary constraint and transfers are large enough to change household choices
fails_when: local spillovers, inflation, or non-recipient effects are ignored
documents.design_implication: Adapt the mechanism to local scarcity, trust, channel, and population constraints before applying it to a new campaign.

documents.title: Gendered Cortisol Dynamics in Cash Transfers
documents.summary: Targeting unconditional cash transfers to women reduced household stress, with evidence suggesting male cortisol fell when female partners received transfers.
documents.text: Cash transfer evidence from Kenya indicates that female recipients experienced improved psychological well-being and household decision-making power. The structured synthesis highlights that stress reductions may also reflect lower male cortisol when women receive transfers, potentially because transfers reduce the provider burden in cohabiting households. This implies that gender-targeted transfers can alter intra-household stress dynamics, not just individual income.
works_when: program design accounts for intra-household power, stress, and provider-role dynamics
fails_when: the household is treated as a single gender-neutral decision unit
documents.design_implication: Treat this as a cautionary case: match behavioral labels and messages with structural support, local trust, and operational capacity before scaling.

documents.title: Sender Salience and Evening Delivery in Digital Credit Reminders
documents.summary: Repayment reminders sent in the evening and reminders identifying peer-to-peer funders significantly increase loan repayment rates.
documents.text: Field evaluations of digital credit and P2P lending platforms in Kenya found evening reminders increased repayment by 8% relative to morning delivery. Listing names or numbers of individual peer funders increased on-time repayment from 27% to 81%, leveraging reciprocity, moral accountability, and attention salience.
documents.effect_size: increased repayment by 8%
works_when: the behavior is socially visible and peers are relevant to the decision
the cue arrives close to the moment of action
fails_when: peer norms substitute for objective feedback or individual accountability
documents.design_implication: Make the target behavior visible to relevant peers, but pair peer pressure with clear accountability when performance quality matters.

documents.title: Labor-as-Agency in Welfare Program Design
documents.summary: Incorporating work requirements in social safety nets improves psychological well-being compared to passive waiting.
documents.text: A 10-day lab-in-the-field experiment with 432 impoverished individuals in Nairobi's Kawangware slum compared daily labor for food vouchers with daily waiting for food vouchers. Labor improved psychological well-being, suggesting agency, dignity, and active contribution matter in welfare design.
works_when: participants can make commitments concrete and revisit them repeatedly
digital attention is weak or cognitive load is high
documents.design_implication: Use concrete commitment artifacts, public accountability, and repeated group rituals to help people protect future intent under present bias.

documents.title: Failure of Light-Touch Positive Psychology Interventions in Scarcity
documents.summary: Low-cost mental framing exercises fail to improve cognitive control, decision-making, or long-term labor supply under scarcity.
documents.text: A 16-day positive psychology intervention in Kenya increased reported gratitude by 0.31 SD but had no meaningful effect on cognitive control, temporal discounting, sleep, aspirations, well-being, or long-term labor supply. Structural and material constraints dominated light-touch cognitive reframing.
documents.effect_size: increased reported gratitude by 0.31 SD
works_when: psychological framing is paired with material support or structural constraint removal
fails_when: light-touch mental framing is expected to overcome severe material scarcity
documents.design_implication: Do not rely on light-touch mindset exercises when material scarcity is the binding constraint; pair psychological support with structural or tangible assistance.

documents.title: Gendered Sensitivity to Workplace Respect and Belongingness
documents.summary: Women show high sensitivity to personalized dignity in the workplace and are more willing to reject high-paying disrespectful work.
documents.text: An experiment with 546 Strathmore University students found gender-mismatched language reduced perceived inclusivity but did not immediately affect short-term task performance. Personalized dignity treatments increased women's dignity index by 0.29 points, and women were more willing than men to refuse disrespectful work even if highly paid.
works_when: workplace design protects dignity, personalization, and inclusion over time
fails_when: short-term productivity metrics hide long-term burnout or exit
documents.design_implication: Measure dignity, inclusion, and willingness to remain over time because short-term task performance can hide slow-burn exclusion costs.

documents.title: Mutual Help Social Norms Shield Low Performance in Classrooms
documents.summary: Strong informal peer-help social norms among teachers are paradoxically correlated with lower instructional performance.
documents.text: An evaluation of Zambia's Catch Up program found that while 86% of teachers reported positive cooperative norms, 58% of teachers who strongly agreed that peers help with challenges were low-performing. Informal cooperative norms can shield low performance unless paired with structured feedback and accountability.
works_when: the behavior is socially visible and peers are relevant to the decision
fails_when: peer norms substitute for objective feedback or individual accountability
documents.design_implication: Make the target behavior visible to relevant peers, but pair peer pressure with clear accountability when performance quality matters.

documents.title: Domestic Labor Friction and Marital Barriers in Female Research Participation
documents.summary: Female research participants face temporal, domestic, and marital constraints that shape lab attendance.
documents.text: Qualitative interviews in Nairobi found female participants spend 3-6 hours daily on unpaid domestic labor, compared to 30 minutes to 2 hours for men. Delayed or late-afternoon sessions can trigger childcare emergencies and marital conflict, especially when women require explicit permission to attend.
works_when: sessions are punctual, childcare-aware, safe for travel, and designed around domestic time constraints
fails_when: participation protocols ignore permission, safety, and unpaid care work
documents.design_implication: Design research sessions around punctuality, childcare, safe travel windows, and household permission constraints to avoid gendered selection bias.

documents.title: Injunctive versus Descriptive Norm Framing for Mobile Banking Deposits
documents.summary: Injunctive norm messages increased deposits among active women by 45%, while descriptive norms drove inactive women.
documents.text: A Nigerian mobile banking intervention used behaviorally informed SMS messages to address low account usage among women. Injunctive norm messages increased deposits among active women from 1.81% to 2.63%, a 45% relative increase. For inactive women, descriptive norm messages increased transfers and payments from 0.09% to 0.38%, showing normative framing must align with account activity status.
documents.effect_size: increased deposits among active women by 45%
works_when: the behavior is socially visible and peers are relevant to the decision
fails_when: digital delivery ignores trust, verification, or access constraints
peer norms substitute for objective feedback or individual accountability
design ignores time poverty, safety, dignity, or household power dynamics
documents.design_implication: Make the target behavior visible to relevant peers, but pair peer pressure with clear accountability when performance quality matters.

documents.title: The Cash-Preferencing Paradox and Agent Trust in Mobile Money Networks
documents.summary: Widespread mobile money adoption in Kenya coexists with high cash preference and localized agent trust networks.
documents.text: Kenyan mobile money users often treat wallets as transactional conduits rather than savings vehicles. Over 90% withdraw cash from agents weekly, 60% keep balances under 1,000 KES, and 53% of deposits route through one preferred agent. Trust remains relational and localized despite digitization.
works_when: trusted local intermediaries or visible verification are available
fails_when: digital delivery ignores trust, verification, or access constraints
documents.design_implication: Build around trusted local intermediaries and visible verification rather than assuming institutional or digital trust is enough.

documents.title: Structural Verification Barriers and Single-Signatory Failures in Savings Group Digitization
documents.summary: Mobile banking digitization can fail for informal savings groups due to trust gaps and complex multi-signatory validation needs.
documents.text: Research with Mwanga Community Bank in rural Tanzania found informal savings groups resisted mobile-based banking because single-signatory withdrawals created embezzlement risks and mobile verification procedures were too complex. Agent banking was preferred because it supported physical, transparent, multi-person validation.
works_when: digital systems preserve shared visibility, multi-person validation, and trusted human mediation
fails_when: single-signatory digital workflows create embezzlement or opacity concerns
documents.design_implication: Build around trusted local intermediaries and visible verification rather than assuming institutional or digital trust is enough.

documents.title: Integrating Customary Solidarity Networks into Social Protection
documents.summary: Formal social protection programs in drylands are strengthened when aligned with customary communal redistributive networks.
documents.text: Qualitative research in northern Kenya analyzed formal cash transfers and livestock insurance alongside customary moral economies. External resilience programs can compete with or displace community-led solidarity networks unless designed to align with mutual-aid and redistributive practices.
works_when: the intervention is adapted to local trust, scarcity, and delivery constraints
documents.design_implication: Adapt the mechanism to local scarcity, trust, channel, and population constraints before applying it to a new campaign.

documents.title: Digital Badges and Social Recognition for Community Health Worker Performance
documents.summary: Non-monetary digital performance badges shared on social networks can boost community health worker self-perception and motivation.
documents.text: A Living Goods partnership awarded top community health workers digital performance badges for WhatsApp sharing. The badges validated work ethic, enhanced self-perception, and were shared with family, suggesting reputational rewards can be amplified through family and peer networks.
works_when: the behavior is socially visible and peers are relevant to the decision
fails_when: peer norms substitute for objective feedback or individual accountability
documents.design_implication: Make the target behavior visible to relevant peers, but pair peer pressure with clear accountability when performance quality matters.

documents.title: Prize-Linked Savings Design and Mobile Betting Heuristics
documents.summary: Prize-linked savings can channel gambling heuristics toward formal savings among Kenyan youth.
documents.text: In Kenya, low-income formal account ownership does not necessarily translate into institutional saving. Prize-linked savings products such as Jang Akiba Smart bundle deposits with probabilistic payouts, using lottery and mobile betting heuristics to encourage formal asset accumulation.
works_when: the intervention is adapted to local trust, scarcity, and delivery constraints
fails_when: digital delivery ignores trust, verification, or access constraints
documents.design_implication: Adapt the mechanism to local scarcity, trust, channel, and population constraints before applying it to a new campaign.

documents.title: Public Health Surveillance App Frictions and Mandatory Quarantine Suspicion
documents.summary: Mobile public health self-assessment uptake is constrained by fears of government tracking and mandatory quarantine.
documents.text: An SMS-based pilot with 3,345 respondents in Kenya during COVID-19 found users feared health self-assessment apps would submit personal data to government and trigger mandatory quarantine. Message fatigue and surveillance concerns created strong trust barriers for digital health tools.
works_when: trusted local intermediaries or visible verification are available
fails_when: digital delivery ignores trust, verification, or access constraints
documents.design_implication: Build around trusted local intermediaries and visible verification rather than assuming institutional or digital trust is enough.

documents.title: SMS Survey Architecture and Completion Rates
documents.summary: Small incentives, length disclosure, and optimized survey design improve SMS survey completion among low-income urban cohorts.
documents.text: Busara research on SMS surveys found completion can rise from about 20% to 30% with optimized delivery and incentives. A 25 KES incentive increased completion by 5-6 percentage points, 100 KES increased long-survey completion by 11 points, and disclosing survey length increased completion by 2 points. Once respondents answer the first question, 94% complete the survey.
documents.effect_size: from about 20% to 30% with optimized delivery and incentives
works_when: trusted local intermediaries or visible verification are available
documents.design_implication: Build around trusted local intermediaries and visible verification rather than assuming institutional or digital trust is enough.

documents.title: Operational Limits of Rapid Humanitarian Behavioral Research
documents.summary: Crisis research is constrained by partnership misalignment, staff turnover, low digital access, shared phones, inattention, and suspicion.
documents.text: Attempts to study and counter misinformation during COVID-19 showed that rapid humanitarian research can stall due to organizational misalignment, field staff burnout, overestimated technological literacy, mobile phone sharing, privacy concerns, and suspicion of official-looking messages. Behavioral interventions in crisis settings need local trust channels and operational realism.
works_when: trusted local intermediaries or visible verification are available
fails_when: digital delivery ignores trust, verification, or access constraints
messages only shift beliefs while practical barriers remain
documents.design_implication: Use local operational partners, analog-digital hybridity, and trust-preserving data practices before deploying mobile-first crisis interventions.

documents.title: Digital Credit APR Transparency and Repayment Framing
documents.summary: Standard APR interest disclosures confuse low-income mobile borrowers, whereas simple total repayment cost in local currency with concrete calendar deadlines increases on-time repayment.
documents.text: When mobile micro-borrowers in Kenya were shown equivalent loan costs in total fee amounts (e.g. 'KES 250 fee on KES 1,000 borrowed') instead of annualized percentages, borrower comprehension jumped by 34pp and default rates decreased by 18%. Reminders framed around avoiding late access penalties had twice the compliance effect of neutral notifications.
documents.effect_size: 18% reduction in 30-day default rates, +34pp comprehension
works_when: the cost is presented in absolute local currency rather than abstract percentage rates
reminders arrive on the exact morning repayment is due
fails_when: the user faces acute absolute liquidity depletion
the credit provider is perceived as predatory
documents.design_implication: Display single total cost figures in local currency and frame repayment around protecting future borrowing access.

documents.title: Mobile Overdraft (Fuliza) Opt-In Friction and Auto-Sweep Restraint
documents.summary: Frictionless auto-approval overdrafts trigger high present bias and overdraft habituation; introducing a mandatory 2-step confirmation prompt reduced impulsive micro-borrowing.
documents.text: In mobile money overdrafts in Kenya, users frequently borrowed small sums to complete discretionary purchases. Introducing a frictionless default accelerated debt cycles, while adding a single friction screen ('Do you want to use Fuliza overdraft for KES 200 with daily fee KES 10?') reduced impulsive transactions by 22% without harming necessary merchant payments.
documents.effect_size: 22% drop in impulsive micro-overdrafts
works_when: friction is placed immediately prior to fund disbursement
daily fee cost is explicitly displayed
fails_when: emergency medical or survival cash needs dominate
documents.design_implication: Introduce deliberative friction and explicit cumulative cost disclosure on digital credit checkout flows.

documents.title: Agent Banking Trust Signaling and Official Photo Verification
documents.summary: In rural and peri-urban Northern Nigeria, distrust of POS/mobile banking agents suppressed formal deposits; standardized branded photo badges and instant SMS receipts boosted deposit volume.
documents.text: Informal customers fear agent fraud and system downtime. Equipping agent banking kiosks with tamper-evident standardized signage, official bank accreditation badges with photo ID, and instant audible SMS confirmation increased first-time customer deposits by 41%.
documents.effect_size: +41% increase in first-time user deposit volumes
works_when: verification credentials are physical, visually prominent, and instantly verifiable by SMS receipt
fails_when: underlying telecom network latency delays the transaction confirmation SMS
documents.design_implication: Reinforce digital agent transactions with high-visibility physical accreditation and instant dual verification receipts.

documents.title: Peer Accountability in Digital Savings Groups (ROSCAs / Chamas)
documents.summary: Digitizing informal savings groups (Chamas) often causes default spikes because physical social pressure is lost; automated WhatsApp group contribution digests restored repayment rates.
documents.text: When groups shifted from weekly in-person meetings to an anonymous mobile app, monthly on-time contributions fell by 31%. Introducing a weekly automated group summary broadcasted into the group's WhatsApp chat ('8 of 10 members contributed this week') leveraged descriptive social norms and restored on-time contributions by 27pp.
documents.effect_size: +27pp recovery in on-time contribution compliance
works_when: contributions are aggregated as group descriptive norms rather than publicly shaming individual names
fails_when: individual naming leads to public humiliation and group dissolution
documents.design_implication: Preserve the social observability of informal group rituals inside digital interfaces using aggregate social progress signals.

documents.title: M-Shwari Lock Savings and Goal-Labeled Digital Sub-Accounts
documents.summary: Allowing mobile depositors to partition funds into labeled digital accounts ('School Fees', 'Emergency') with self-imposed withdrawal lock periods increased 6-month savings balances by 82%.
documents.text: Evaluation of Safaricom M-Shwari Lock Savings demonstrated that psychological mental accounting shields cash from daily demands by kin and impulsive spending. When users selected their own unlock date and goal label, savings persistence doubled compared to general interest-bearing savings accounts.
documents.effect_size: +82% higher total average savings balance after 6 months
works_when: users actively choose the commitment horizon and the goal label has high personal affective value
fails_when: emergency liquidity shocks force users into costly informal borrowing because funds are locked
documents.design_implication: Provide goal-labeled sub-wallets with flexible commitment locks and clear visual progress meters.

documents.title: Incentivized Maternal Clinic Delivery and Antenatal Care Adherence
documents.summary: Small, non-cash in-kind incentives delivered at maternal health visits combined with tailored SMS reminders doubled completed 4-visit antenatal schedules.
documents.text: In Western Kenya, providing expectant mothers with a bundle of essential newborn care items (mama kits: basin, swaddling cloth, soap) upon completing four antenatal visits increased clinic birth delivery rates from 39% to 78%. SMS reminders sent 48 hours prior to scheduled visits amplified clinic show-up rates by an additional 14pp.
documents.effect_size: Antenatal completion doubled; clinic births rose from 39% to 78%
works_when: incentives are immediate, non-monetary items tied directly to child well-being
reminders include the clinic nurse's name
fails_when: transportation costs to remote clinics exceed the perceived value of the in-kind incentive
documents.design_implication: Bundle high-utility maternity care items with timely SMS reminders that humanize clinic staff.

documents.title: Social Recognition Badges vs. Financial Bonuses for Community Health Volunteers
documents.summary: Public recognition of Community Health Promoters (CHPs) at monthly village assemblies drove higher household visitation rates than equivalent cash bonuses.
documents.text: Comparing non-monetary social recognition (public certificates and village leader commendation) against variable financial performance bonuses for community health promoters across 120 villages showed that public status recognition sustained 28% higher home health visits over 9 months, whereas small cash bonuses suffered from motivational crowding-out once discontinued.
documents.effect_size: +28% higher sustained household visit rates over 9 months
works_when: social status is meaningful within the localized village hierarchy
fails_when: health workers lack basic supplies or face acute personal poverty where baseline income is insufficient
documents.design_implication: Prioritize institutional and community social status recognition to sustain community health agent performance.

documents.title: Point-of-Collection Free Chlorine Dispensers for Drinking Water
documents.summary: Installing free, conveniently situated chlorine dispensers directly beside communal water points boosted water treatment rates from 10% to over 60%.
documents.text: Providing free water treatment tablets to homes led to rapid attrition (<15% long-term use) due to daily cognitive friction and forgetting. Placing bright blue chlorine dispensers directly at natural water collection points turned treatment into a public, automatic habit at the moment of filling jerrycans, maintaining >60% adoption for over 3 years.
documents.effect_size: Water treatment increased from 10% to 61% sustained over 3 years
works_when: chlorine is free, hardware is installed at the exact point of jerrycan filling, and lever pull is visible to peers
fails_when: dispensers run out of chemical supply or break down without local maintenance
documents.design_implication: Design physical environmental defaults at the geographic choke-point of habit execution.

documents.title: Child Immunization Reminder Timing: Morning-of vs. Day-Before SMS
documents.summary: SMS immunization reminders sent at 7:00 AM on the day of the clinic increased vaccination completion by 16pp, whereas 48-hour advance notices were forgotten.
documents.text: In an RCT across clinics in Kano State, Nigeria, sending SMS alerts 2 days prior to scheduled infant vaccine dates had negligible impact (+3pp), as mothers experienced rapid temporal decay of attention. Shifting the automated SMS to 7:00 AM on the clinic morning increased attendance by 16pp.
documents.effect_size: +16pp increase in on-time vaccination completion
works_when: message arrives early morning before the caregiver plans the daily market/farm itinerary
fails_when: clinic stock-outs or vaccine shortages cause mothers who attend to be turned away
documents.design_implication: Align nudge timing with the morning moment of daily schedule formation rather than multi-day advance notice.

documents.title: Messenger Credibility in Routine Immunization: Religious and Traditional Leaders
documents.summary: Endorsements recorded by respected local Emirs and Imams in Northern Nigeria increased child vaccine acceptance by 33%, whereas state health ministry broadcasts generated skepticism.
documents.text: Due to low baseline institutional trust in public authorities, centralized government health messaging was met with apathy or suspicion of covert agendas. Replacing ministry spokesperson audio with 30-second localized radio messages and loudspeaker announcements from recognized community and religious leaders lifted vaccine coverage by 33%.
documents.effect_size: +33% increase in routine immunization uptake
works_when: messengers are recognized local religious authorities speaking in local dialects
fails_when: the message sounds scripted or appears overly coached by foreign donors or central government
documents.design_implication: Shift campaign messengers from impersonal institutional brands to high-credibility local traditional or spiritual authorities.

documents.title: Harvest-Time Pre-Commitment Vouchers for Smallholder Fertilizer Adoption
documents.summary: Offering smallholder farmers the opportunity to buy fertilizer vouchers immediately after harvestâ€”when cash is liquidâ€”increased planting season fertilizer use by 14pp.
documents.text: The SAFI model demonstrated that farmers genuinely intend to invest in fertilizer for the next season, but by planting time cash has dissipated. Offering free delivery and pre-purchase vouchers immediately after harvest increased adoption by 14pp, achieving higher investment than heavy subsidies offered at planting season.
documents.effect_size: +14pp higher fertilizer adoption without ongoing subsidy
works_when: the offer is made during the 2-3 week post-harvest window when crops have been sold for cash
fails_when: immediate emergency cash needs (school fees) drain post-harvest funds before the voucher agent arrives
documents.design_implication: Synchronize agricultural investment nudges with seasonal cash liquidity peaks rather than input utilization dates.

documents.title: Social Contagion and Visual Demonstration in Drought-Tolerant Maize Adoption
documents.summary: Locating demonstration plots along frequently walked village footpaths accelerated drought-tolerant seed adoption 3x faster than centralized workshops.
documents.text: Farmers are risk-averse to new hybrid seed claims. Setting up small, roadside test plots labeled with simple signboards showing maize vigor under drought conditions allowed peer farmers to observe crop resilience during their daily commute, tripling commercial seed purchases compared to traditional extension seminars.
documents.effect_size: 3x increase in adoption rate of drought-tolerant seed varieties
works_when: plots are placed in high-visibility transit points and maintained by ordinary local peers
fails_when: demonstration plots are perceived to receive subsidized water, fertilizers, or exceptional expert care
documents.design_implication: Rely on unobtrusive, high-observability public demonstrations where users observe peer success naturally.

documents.title: Opt-Out Default Bundling of Weather Index Micro-Insurance
documents.summary: Bundling drought and excess rainfall index micro-insurance directly into certified seed bags as an automatic default increased insurance coverage from 4% to 89%.
documents.text: Voluntary index insurance suffers from severe cognitive friction and basis risk mistrust, resulting in dismal take-up (<5%). When insurance was bundled into the seed package price with a scratch-off SMS registration code on the bag, coverage surged to 89%, protecting smallholders from severe drought-induced asset sales.
documents.effect_size: Insurance coverage jumped from 4% to 89% via bundled default
works_when: registration requires only a single free SMS scratch code and claims payout is automated via mobile money
fails_when: pay-out criteria are opaque and satellite triggers fail to register localized hail or pest damage
documents.design_implication: Embed protective financial and climate mechanisms into existing physical purchase flows as default features.

documents.title: Pictorial Heuristic Soil Health Cards vs. Complex Laboratory Data
documents.summary: Replacing numeric laboratory chemical values (pH, ppm Nitrogen) with color-coded traffic light charts and simple bag recommendations increased correct fertilizer application by 47%.
documents.text: Technical soil tests overwhelmed smallholder farmers with cognitive load, resulting in zero behavioral change. Redesigning results into a simple pictorial card ('Red = Needs 1 bag of Lime; Green = Normal') increased adoption of corrective soil amendments from 12% to 59%.
documents.effect_size: 47pp increase in correct soil management practices
works_when: recommendations are translated into local physical units (e.g. 50kg bags per acre) and intuitive color codes
fails_when: recommended input types are unavailable in local agro-dealer shops
documents.design_implication: Translate complex technical diagnostic data into actionable visual rules of thumb.

documents.title: Hermetic Grain Storage Bag Demonstrations at Market Days
documents.summary: Live knife puncture and oxygen depletion demonstrations of hermetic storage bags at rural market fairs overcame skepticism regarding chemical-free grain preservation.
documents.text: Smallholders were accustomed to using chemical dusts to preserve maize against weevils and distrusted plastic triple-layer hermetic bags. Live interactive market demonstrations where farmers inspected 6-month-old weevil-free maize stored without chemicals increased purchase of storage bags by 53%.
documents.effect_size: +53% increase in adoption of hermetic storage bags
works_when: farmers physically touch and smell the preserved grain and witness live airtight sealing
fails_when: counterfeit imitation bags flood the local market and tear easily, undermining product reputation
documents.design_implication: Address skepticism toward novel technological substitutes through experiential, sensory demonstration.

documents.title: Teaching at the Right Level (TaRL): Teacher Behavioral Coaching and Peer Cohorts
documents.summary: Pairing primary school teachers in Zambia with peer coaching WhatsApp cohorts and simple daily diagnostic checklists increased remedial teaching delivery compliance by 38pp.
documents.text: Teachers often abandon remedial pedagogy because it deviates from standard curricula. Implementing weekly peer check-in prompts on mobile and lightweight pictorial student tracking cards kept teachers accountable, lifting remedial learning class delivery from 42% to 80%.
documents.effect_size: +38pp increase in verified delivery of remedial learning sessions
works_when: supervisors provide encouraging peer mentorship rather than bureaucratic inspections
fails_when: teachers are overburdened by mandatory standardized testing administrative requirements
documents.design_implication: Use peer reflection circles and low-friction mobile checklists to sustain pedagogical compliance.

documents.title: Weekly Bite-Sized Parental SMS Prompts for Early Childhood Literacy
documents.summary: Sending low-income mothers three bite-sized, actionable learning game prompts per week via SMS increased home learning time by 2.4 hours weekly.
documents.text: Parents in low-income informal settlements in Nairobi felt unqualified to support learning at home. Weekly SMS prompts suggesting zero-cost everyday games ('Ask your child to count the tomatoes you bought at the market today') removed intimidation and boosted home engagement by 2.4 hours/week.
documents.effect_size: +2.4 hours/week increase in interactive parent-child learning activity
works_when: prompts integrate into routine household chores without requiring books or formal schooling
fails_when: activities assume quiet study space or parental literacy in English
documents.design_implication: Break educational parental support into micro-behaviors embedded within daily domestic routines.

documents.title: Social Accountability and Peer Recognition in Teacher Attendance
documents.summary: Posting weekly teacher attendance summaries in the school staffroom combined with community acknowledgement lifted attendance rates from 71% to 89%.
documents.text: In rural primary schools, top-down biometric attendance monitoring sparked teacher resentment and work-to-rule strikes. Shifting to an affirmative peer recognition board ('Celebrating our 100% on-time educators this week') paired with monthly PTA appreciation notes improved teacher attendance without administrative hostility.
documents.effect_size: Attendance increased from 71% to 89%
works_when: the system highlights positive achievement rather than publishing punitive shaming lists
fails_when: chronic teacher absenteeism is driven by months of delayed government salary disbursements
documents.design_implication: Harness positive social observability and status recognition rather than punitive surveillance.

documents.title: Contextualized Growth Mindset in Low-Resource African Classrooms
documents.summary: Adapting growth mindset narratives to emphasize community role models and resilient problem-solving improved secondary student academic persistence by 0.22 SD.
documents.text: Direct translations of Western growth mindset texts failed because students attributed low grades to structural poverty. Adapting exercises to showcase local African figures who overcame resource scarcity by seeking peer study groups boosted STEM exam scores by 0.22 SD at negligible cost.
documents.effect_size: 0.22 standard deviation increase in end-of-term academic performance
works_when: narratives validate socioeconomic realities while highlighting agency in collective study routines
fails_when: teachers explicitly label struggling students as incapable of improvement
documents.design_implication: Ground cognitive mindset reframing in authentic cultural narratives of communal resilience.

documents.title: Informal Market Stall Tax Compliance via Visible Service Reciprocity
documents.summary: Informal market traders in Kano and Lagos increased municipal fee compliance by 34% when letters highlighted immediate tangible market renovations rather than legal penalties.
documents.text: Informal traders view tax authorities as extortionary. Framing local government levies around explicit reciprocal investments ('Your market ticket pays for the new borehole and night security guards in Zone 3') accompanied by on-site progress banners dramatically increased voluntary tax ticket payments.
documents.effect_size: +34% increase in voluntary market fee ticket purchases
works_when: the promised public good is hyper-local, physical, and verifiable within 30 days
fails_when: traders see market revenue diverted or no physical improvements materialize after 60 days
documents.design_implication: Establish psychological reciprocity contracts by linking citizen payments to visible, hyper-local public works.

documents.title: Municipal Property Tax: Public Service Attribution ('Your Tax Repaired This Road')
documents.summary: Sending SMS notifications that attributed specific completed infrastructure projects to local council tax revenue lifted annual property tax compliance by 8.4pp.
documents.text: Standard legal threat letters ('Pay immediately or face property confiscation') trigger psychological reactance and avoidance in emerging market cities. Replacing threats with transparency statements demonstrating road grading and flood gutter construction improved compliance by 8.4pp and lowered taxpayer disputes.
documents.effect_size: +8.4pp increase in on-time municipal property tax payments
works_when: taxpayers can directly see and benefit from the referenced public infrastructure project
fails_when: citizens perceive high-level embezzlement among municipal executives
documents.design_implication: Counter institutional cynicism with specific, verifiable evidence of tax-funded public benefits.

documents.title: Anonymous WhatsApp Voice Note Reporting in Local Governance
documents.summary: Providing an anonymous WhatsApp channel accepting voice notes in local languages increased citizen service failure and corruption reports by 400% compared to web forms.
documents.text: Traditional grievance redressing portals require high digital literacy, written English, and personal identification, creating severe friction and fear of retaliation. Launching a dedicated WhatsApp number that welcomed short voice notes in Nigerian Pidgin or Yoruba eliminated friction and multiplied civic reporting.
documents.effect_size: 400% increase in civic service complaint and feedback submissions
works_when: citizens receive an immediate automated confirmation guaranteeing voice pitch masking and anonymization
fails_when: authorities fail to resolve or acknowledge reported issues, generating reporting fatigue
documents.design_implication: Lower civic reporting friction by embracing vernacular voice messaging and ironclad anonymity protections.

documents.title: Neighborhood Cleanliness Pledges and Public Verification Badges
documents.summary: Distributing publicly visible storefront verification stickers upon participating in monthly sanitation clean-ups sustained 91% community waste compliance.
documents.text: Relying on municipal enforcement against illegal dumping in informal settlements yielded low compliance. Creating a neighborhood cleanliness pledge where shopkeepers who kept their gutter clear received a bright green 'Clean Business Leader' sticker created a descriptive peer norm and reduced dumping.
documents.effect_size: 91% sustained cleanliness compliance across audited commercial lanes
works_when: badges are awarded by trusted community elders during visible public walk-throughs
fails_when: municipal waste collection trucks fail to empty designated neighborhood dumpsters
documents.design_implication: Transform unseen civic compliance into public, socially observable status symbols.

documents.title: Women's Mobile Money Account Privacy and Kinship Shielding
documents.summary: Giving female micro-entrepreneurs private mobile money sub-wallets shielded their business earnings from family appropriation, boosting business reinvestment by 38%.
documents.text: Women in East Africa experience intense 'kinship tax'â€”social pressure to share liquid cash with husbands and extended family. Providing private digital accounts protected by private PINs and secret SMS balance inquiries allowed female traders to accumulate capital, increasing business inventory investments by 38% and profits by 22%.
documents.effect_size: +38% increase in business capital reinvestment, +22% profit lift
works_when: balance notifications and account statements can be hidden or muted from household view
fails_when: domestic violence or physical phone confiscation compromises device privacy
documents.design_implication: Incorporate privacy safeguards into digital wallets to protect vulnerable earners from intra-household financial drain.

documents.title: Gendered Time Poverty: Overcoming Scheduling Frictions in Training Programs
documents.summary: Rescheduling agricultural and digital skills workshops to mid-afternoon hours and offering on-site childcare increased female participation from 23% to 68%.
documents.text: Morning training sessions clashed with peak female domestic labor (cooking, fetching water, child preparation). Shifting sessions to 2:00 PM and providing safe communal childcare eliminated structural frictions and tripled female attendance.
documents.effect_size: Female program participation increased from 23% to 68%
works_when: timing respects the daily gendered division of domestic and care labor
fails_when: spouses withhold permission for women to travel outside the immediate village
documents.design_implication: Audit and dismantle gendered time poverty and caregiving frictions before designing behavioral interventions.

documents.title: In-Kind Asset Delivery vs. Cash Grants for Female Micro-Enterprises
documents.summary: Delivering business capital as direct physical inventory (fabrics, sewing equipment) rather than cash doubled long-term profitability for female-owned enterprises in Ghana.
documents.text: While unconditional cash grants generated high returns for male entrepreneurs, women's cash grants were frequently captured by household subsistence emergencies or family demands. Delivering capital in the form of business inventory insulated the grant from domestic redirection, yielding double the business profit growth.
documents.effect_size: 104% higher business profit growth compared to equivalent liquid cash
works_when: the physical asset matches the entrepreneur's existing trade and cannot be easily liquidated at distress prices
fails_when: the entrepreneur urgently needs working capital to cover urgent supplier payables
documents.design_implication: Use in-kind physical asset provisioning to shield vulnerable female capital from non-business appropriation.

documents.title: Assertiveness Coaching and Mandated Quotas in Community Water Committees
documents.summary: Combining mandated female representation with pre-meeting assertiveness practice increased female speaking time by 4x and improved community water maintenance.
documents.text: Simply mandating gender quotas on local water user committees led to symbolic 'tokenism', where women attended but remained silent. Pre-meeting group roleplay coaching where women practiced voicing maintenance objections increased actual meeting participation 4-fold and reduced borehole downtime by 45%.
documents.effect_size: 4x increase in female active speaking time; 45% faster borehole repair times
works_when: coaching builds solidarity among female members before they enter mixed-gender community forums
fails_when: entrenched patriarchal village leadership retaliates outside the formal committee setting
documents.design_implication: Pair structural inclusion quotas with targeted psychological empowerment and behavioral preparation.

documents.title: The Cognitive Tax of Poverty: Experimental Proof from Nairobi
documents.summary: Acute financial worry consumes mental bandwidth, temporarily reducing fluid intelligence and executive function by up to 13 IQ points equivalent.
documents.text: Busara laboratory experiments in Nairobi with low-income residents showed that prompting people with high unexpected monetary expenses (e.g. medical emergencies) caused a marked drop in cognitive performance on Raven's matrices and Stroop tasks among the poor, but not among higher-income peers. This bandwidth tax causes poor individuals to forget appointments and make seemingly short-sighted financial choices.
documents.effect_size: Cognitive capacity reduction equivalent to 13 IQ points under acute scarcity
works_when: financial strain is made psychologically salient
fails_when: basic financial security is guaranteed through steady cash flow or buffer assets
documents.design_implication: Radically simplify information, cut steps, and avoid demanding complex calculations from people living under poverty.

documents.title: Cortisol, Biological Stress, and Steep Temporal Discounting
documents.summary: Elevated cortisol from economic instability directly accelerates temporal discounting, explaining why long-term savings or health investments are deprioritized.
documents.text: Biomarker analysis conducted in informal settlements revealed a biological link between chronic poverty stress (measured in salivary cortisol) and high discount rates for future financial payoffs. Providing unconditional cash transfers reduced stress biomarkers and restored willingness to choose larger, delayed economic rewards.
documents.effect_size: Significant reduction in present-bias discounting following stress-reducing liquidity
works_when: financial transfers are unconditional and large enough to alleviate existential dread
fails_when: stress stems from physical insecurity or severe chronic health crises rather than cash alone
documents.design_implication: Frontload tangible immediate payoffs rather than asking scarcity-burdened audiences to wait for delayed future benefits.

documents.title: Sludge Auditing in Social Cash Transfer Enrollment: Nigeria NASSP
documents.summary: Eliminating redundant biometric re-verification and paper documentation hurdles reduced enrollment drop-out among poorest rural beneficiaries by 52%.
documents.text: In the Nigeria National Social Safety Net Program, vulnerable beneficiaries were dropping out due to bureaucratic friction ('sludge'): walking multiple miles to repeated registration points with paper photocopies. Streamlining verification into a single community-based enumerator visit boosted completed enrollment from 48% to 94%.
documents.effect_size: Enrollment completion rose from 48% to 94%; 52% reduction in attrition
works_when: verification is brought directly to the village center with offline-capable biometric devices
fails_when: fraud detection concerns lead administrators to re-introduce centralized paperwork
documents.design_implication: Audit and remove administrative sludge that imposes steep travel, document, and cognitive costs on the poor.

documents.title: Simplifying Agricultural Subsidy E-Vouchers at Agro-Dealer POS
documents.summary: Simplifying 12-digit USSD voucher codes into a 4-digit PIN with audio confirmation reduced farmer redemption failures from 29% to under 3%.
documents.text: Smallholder farmers redeeming government fertilizer subsidies faced complex USSD menus with 12-digit alphanumeric codes on basic phones, causing high entry timeouts and merchant frustration. Simplifying redemption to a short 4-digit PIN paired with an automated dealer voice confirmation reduced transaction abandonment by 90%.
documents.effect_size: Redemption failure rate collapsed from 29% to 2.8%
works_when: codes are short, numeric, and feedback is auditory for semi-literate users
fails_when: local cellular base stations experience prolonged power outages
documents.design_implication: Design digital transactional rails for the lowest-capability device and the lowest-literacy user.
